parsed.explanation: Combined regime imposes tier-1 universal exposures: federal binary-document and government-facility rules, entry refusal and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility for document/sex discrepancy, and birth-sex custody with documented hormone removal, forced labour and sexual abuse if detained. Courts, injunctions, litigation and this division's lack of an adult statewide bathroom ban provide real but incomplete recourse. A travelling minor faces an operative care and school-facility ban. No execution or routine imprisonment for presence is documented, but outed travellers risk exclusion, detention, humiliation and severe custody harm.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal binary sex definition; X/mismatched passports no longer issued, Supreme Court allowed restriction. Entry cable: discrepancy/doubt on sex requires refusal and more evidence; suspected wilful misrepresentation may support permanent lifetime fraud ineligibility.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, limited waivers exist, and passport policy is being litigated.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can escalate from refusal to fraud investigation, detention and birth-sex custody placement.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections adopted conversion-style policies including hair cutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse; trespass arrestee held 24 hours in men's ward.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Courts have enjoined some orders; habeas and other remedies not specifically documented for detained visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest for facilities trespass or immigration detention exposes traveller to birth-sex placement and documented custodial abuse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity. Many states ban such use; four make it criminal in defined circumstances, requiring wilful entry plus refusal to depart.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This division documents no statewide adult bathroom/facility rule; its 2023 restriction applies to public-school students, with district implementation.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facilities, schools and other government buildings remain exposed even where the division has no adult statewide ban.

care_services.exposure: Division bans puberty blockers and hormones for transgender minors, in force since July 2023 with no phase-out. National orders target minor care and proposed rules would bar public insurance under 18.
care_services.protection: Care ban was challenged and appeals allowed it to remain while litigation proceeds; adult care ban is not documented. Emergency care treatment is not documented.
care_services.interaction: A minor traveller may be denied continuing medication; hospital or clinic discovery can lead to records, reporting and family separation risks.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal measures direct investigation/prosecution over school gender-ideology and social transition, restrict sports and funding, and 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises groups described as radically pro-transgender.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Several orders have been blocked or enjoined; national hate-crime law covers gender identity, but this division's hate-crime statute expressly excludes gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat framing increases police scrutiny and makes local recourse uneven, especially outside the 19 municipalities with ordinances.

minors_guardians.exposure: School bathrooms restricted to birth-assigned sex, school sport closed to transgender girls, minor medical care banned without phase-out. Federal order directs criminal investigation of teachers facilitating social transition including names/pronouns.
minors_guardians.protection: Ban challenges remain in litigation and status since September 2023 is uncertain; guardians' own legal exposure is not documented beyond facilitation language.
minors_guardians.interaction: Parent/guardian travel with a minor risks school exclusion, care denial and scrutiny of efforts to support the child's identity.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence statistics documented for this division. Nationally, only 23 states cover gender identity in bias-violence statutes; 2025 polling shows 66% support birth-sex listing on documents. Airport screening can be invasive and outing.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute, 2018 appellate employment protection, 2008 state-employee executive order and 19 municipal ordinances provide patchwork recourse.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Patchwork protections mean street, transport and service responses vary sharply by municipality and federal setting.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit, challenges to executive orders and proposed health rules unresolved; corrections bureau stopped reporting transgender prisoner numbers from 2025; enforcement of school facility provision unquantified.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts have issued injunctions and appellate rulings; civil-liberties litigation and legal-aid guidance are active.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies may operate after refusal, arrest or care denial but often too slowly to prevent travel disruption or custody harm.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in that exclusion, discretionary state action and ineffective immediate remedy are central, but this case adds custody abuse and potential lifetime immigration ineligibility, suggesting comparable or slightly lower safety.
Lower than 0.45-A because universal federal facility/document exposure is combined with documented severe custody practices and a minor care ban, not only verification, humiliation and denial.

Much lower than 0.65-A: there, brief detention ended in release, apology and compensation under reliable courts; here, restrictions are federally operative, Supreme Court-allowed in part, and custody harm is documented.

parsed.synthesis: The operative system is federal document/facility restrictions interacting with state school and minor-care bans, while division-level adult facilities and municipal ordinances offer only partial shelter. Courts and litigation moderate but do not neutralise exposure: an outed adult risks refusal, investigation, trespass arrest or birth-sex custody; a minor additionally faces school and care exclusion. Severity if detained is high, though death and routine imprisonment for presence are not documented.
